h1: The 13 Best Monitor Privacy Screens Under $150 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Privacy Screens Under $150: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 13 monitor privacy filters scored on viewing angle, fit data and finish, from 24-inch pairs to a 15.6-inch laptop screen.
summary: The Vxaop 27-inch 2-pack is the pick: it publishes a 60 degree viewing cone and a matte anti-glare coating, and ships two filters. For a 24-inch panel, the Peslv 2-pack adds a reversible surface. If you want exact fit numbers, Mamol and Syhauifei print their dimensions. Laptop users should look at the PYS magnetic filter.
intro: Every privacy filter in this group costs well under $150, so price is not the question. The real question is whether the listing lets you check fit and performance before you buy. A filter cut a few millimetres too small leaves a bright border, and one with no stated viewing angle is a guess.

We ranked thirteen filters on what their spec sheets actually say: viewing cone, finish, published dimensions, pack size and mounting. Sized to 24 and 27 inch monitors, plus one laptop model, they fit most desks.

products.name: Vxaop 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Screen Filter
products.verdict: The one listing here that publishes its viewing angle, glare coating and blue light claim.
products.description:
Vxaop is the most specific spec sheet in this group. It states a 60 degree viewing cone, an anti-glare matte coating and a 95 percent blue light reduction claim, and it ships as a pair for 27-inch 16:9 monitors. Most rivals tell you a screen is dark from the side and stop there.

It ranks first because you can verify what you are buying before you click. The 27-inch pairs from Peslv and Mamol cover the same size, but their listings lean on marketing language and an unnamed optical supplier. The tradeoff is that a matte coating softens the picture slightly, which photo editors will notice.

Buy it if you work in an open office or share a desk and want a 27-inch filter with numbers behind it. Skip it if you need colour-critical work.
cons: Blue light claim is the maker's own
products.skipIf: You edit photos or video and need perfect colour.

products.name: Peslv 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Screen
products.verdict: A reversible 27-inch pair with a stated 92 percent light-filtering figure.
products.description:
Peslv sells a pair of 27-inch filters with a double-sided surface, so one face can be glossy and the other matte. The listing says its optical film is imported from Japan and filters out 92 percent of light at the side angles, and it claims a fit modelled on a real machine.

It sits just under Vxaop because the listing gives no viewing angle in degrees, so the privacy claim is harder to compare, and it costs more. Against the Mamol 27-inch pair below, the reversible surface is the real advantage, since you can swap finishes if glare turns out worse than expected.

A good choice for a 27-inch screen near a window where you may want to try both finishes. Treat the 92 percent figure as the seller's claim.
products.idealFor: People near windows who want to try two finishes.
products.skipIf: You want a published viewing angle.

products.name: Protescreen 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Screen
products.verdict: A plain 27-inch pair from a seller that says it has revised the design 200 times.
products.description:
Protescreen supplies two 27-inch filters for 16:9 widescreen monitors. The seller says the design has gone through 200 updates, which is a claim about iteration, not about how well the film performs.

It ranks below Peslv and Vxaop because the listing offers fewer measurable specs, so you are choosing on trust. Its strength is the simple two-piece pack for a standard 27-inch panel, which keeps the cost per screen low if you outfit two desks.

Pick it if you want a no-fuss 27-inch pair and accept less detail. Check your exact panel dimensions first, since filters are cut to size.
cons: Fit depends on exact panel size
products.skipIf: You want a stated viewing angle.

products.name: Mamol 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Filter
products.verdict: Lists exact panel dimensions so you can match your monitor before ordering.
products.description:
Mamol prints the fit dimensions for its 27-inch filter: 23 9/16 by 13 1/4 inches, or 598 by 337 mm. It markets the screen as blacking out content from the side and reducing eye strain.

That dimension line is the reason it outranks several thinner listings. You can lay a tape across your panel and confirm a match. It trails Peslv because there is no reversible surface and no stated filtering percentage.

Good for buyers who are nervous about fit. Measure the visible area first, then compare to the listing.
products.skipIf: Your monitor is not a standard 16:9.

products.name: Magicmoon 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Filter
products.verdict: A 24-inch pair aimed squarely at shared and open work spaces.
products.description:
Magicmoon sells two 24-inch filters for 16:9 monitors, measured diagonally. The listing says the filter makes the screen appear dark when viewed from the side and pitches it for open work spaces.

It leads the 24-inch pairs on clarity of purpose, but it publishes fewer numbers than the Syhauifei or Peslv 24-inch options. The brand notes it fits 24-inch screens only, so a 23.8 or 25 inch panel needs a different filter.

Choose it for a crowded office desk where the main goal is stopping neighbours reading your screen.
products.skipIf: Your panel is not exactly 24 inches.

products.name: Syhauifei 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Screen
products.verdict: Micro-louver film with full 24-inch dimensions and mounting included.
products.description:
Syhauifei uses what it calls an upgraded micro-louver film and lists its 24-inch fit as 609.6 mm diagonal, 532 mm wide and 299 mm tall. Two simple mounting options come with the pair.

Printed dimensions put it ahead of Magicmoon for fit confidence. It ranks below the Peslv 24-inch because that listing adds a reversible surface and a light-filtering figure. The micro-louver design is a common privacy approach, so expect some darkening for you too.

Buy it if you want published dimensions and flexible mounting on a 24-inch screen.
products.idealFor: 24-inch users who want to confirm fit first.

products.name: Peslv 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Screen
products.verdict: The 24-inch twin of the Peslv 27, with a reversible face.
products.description:
Peslv's 24-inch pair repeats the 27-inch formula: a double-sided surface, optical film said to be imported from Japan, and a 92 percent light-filtering claim.

It carries the strongest 24-inch spec sheet here, yet it lands lower than the 27-inch version because it costs noticeably more than the 24-inch rivals. Compared with the Mamol 24-inch, the reversible face is the difference.

Pick it if you want to test glossy and matte on a 24-inch monitor.

products.name: Mamol 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Filter
products.verdict: A simple 24-inch pair that prints its width as 532 mm.
products.description:
Mamol lists its 24-inch filter width as 20 15/16 inches, or 532 mm, and says it blacks out content from the side and eases eye strain.

It matches the Syhauifei on width but lacks mounting detail and film description, so it ranks lower. Against the 27-inch Mamol it is the same product in a smaller cut.

Fine for a basic 24-inch fit without extras.
products.skipIf: You want reversible or published angles.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch Privacy Screen Filter
products.verdict: A single 24-inch multi-layer film filter, not a pair.
products.description:
SightPro sells one filter for a 24-inch 16:9 monitor, listed at 532 by 299 mm. It describes a multi-layered film that blacks out the screen from the side.

It ranks lower than the 2-packs because you get one filter, so a second desk costs a second purchase. It is, though, the simplest way to protect a single 24-inch monitor.

Buy it for one monitor only.

products.name: Hanging Removable 24 Inch Privacy Screen 2-Pack
products.verdict: A hanging design that skips adhesive and installs quickly.
products.description:
This pair hangs on the monitor instead of sticking on, so it is removable. The listing gives 547 by 320 mm and says that unlike adhesive filters it does not need an exact fit.

It ranks mid-table because removability matters only if you share a screen, and it is the priciest 24-inch pair here. The larger size, 547 by 320 mm, suits monitors with thicker bezels.

Choose it if you want to take the filter off for presentations.
products.idealFor: Shared screens that need the filter off at times.

products.name: PYS Magnetic Laptop Privacy Screen 15.6 Inch
products.verdict: The only laptop filter here, attaching magnetically and not for touchscreens.
products.description:
PYS makes a magnetic privacy filter for 15.6-inch 16:9 laptops. The listing stresses easy installation by magnet and glare reduction, and warns that it is not optimized for touchscreens.

It ranks near the bottom only because it targets a different device from the monitor filters. For laptops it is the one that matters here.

Buy it for a non-touch 15.6-inch laptop used in cafes or on trips.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter 24 Inch 16:9
products.verdict: A reversible single 24-inch filter, with visible area stated as 532 by 299 mm.
products.description:
This 24-inch filter lists a visible display area of 532 by 299 mm and is reversible, letting you choose glossy or matte. The listing notes it does not block visibility directly behind you.

It sits at the bottom of the monitor group due to thin detail, but reversibility is rare at this price.

Reasonable for one 24-inch monitor if you want a choice of finish.
cons: Does not block view from behind
products.idealFor: One 24-inch monitor with a choice of finish.
products.skipIf: You need privacy from directly behind.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter 27 Inch 16:9
products.verdict: The 27-inch sibling, 598 by 337 mm and reversible.
products.description:
The 27-inch version lists a visible area of 598 by 337 mm and the same reversible finish as the 24-inch.

It ranks last because the listing is thin and offers a single filter. Against the Vxaop pair it gives up numbers and quantity.

Only worth it as a single-screen budget option.
products.idealFor: One 27-inch monitor on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want a pair or published angles.

methodology.title: Published viewing angle
methodology.description: Filters that state a viewing cone in degrees scored above those that only say the screen looks dark from the side.

methodology.title: Fit data
methodology.description: We rewarded listings that print exact width and height, since a wrong cut leaves a visible gap.

methodology.title: Finish choice
methodology.description: Reversible glossy and matte surfaces earned credit because glare varies by room.

methodology.title: Pack value
methodology.description: Two filters per pack beat a single filter at similar size, judged against the other listings in this guide.

methodology.title: Install method
methodology.description: Magnetic, hanging and film mounting each suit different use, so we ranked each against its own purpose.

whatMatters.factor: Measure the visible area, not the diagonal
whatMatters.detail: Filters are cut to a specific width and height, so two 24-inch monitors can differ by several millimetres. Measure the visible panel without the bezel, then compare to the listing, such as 532 by 299 mm for a common 24-inch 16:9.

The viewing cone sets how far from centre a neighbour can still read your screen. A narrower cone, like the 60 degrees on the Vxaop listing, hides more but also narrows your own comfortable seating. Look for a degree figure, not just the word dark.
Matte cuts window reflections but slightly softens text. Glossy keeps sharpness and shows glare. Reversible filters let you test both, which matters if you sit near a window.

Every filter here fits 16:9. An ultrawide or a 16:10 monitor will not fit. Touchscreens are another limit, as the PYS laptop filter says it is not optimized for them. Check your panel's ratio in its specs.

Adhesive-free hanging and magnetic filters come off for presentations, while film filters sit flush. Decide whether you need to remove it often, then choose between the hanging pair and a flush option.

cards.label: Hanging or magnetic
cards.text: Comes off in seconds for screen sharing or a meeting. It sits slightly proud of the panel. Picks: Hanging Removable 24 Inch Privacy Screen 2-Pack and PYS Magnetic Laptop Privacy Screen 15.6 Inch.

cards.label: Flush film
cards.text: Looks cleaner and stays put, but removal is a hassle. Picks: Vxaop 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Screen Filter, Peslv 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Screen and Mamol 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Filter.

howToChoose.note: Default to flush film unless you present from the same screen often.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A stated viewing angle, a matte coating for overhead lights and a fit to your exact panel.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Vxaop 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Screen Filter. It publishes a 60 degree cone and a matte coating, and the Magicmoon 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Filter is the simpler choice for a smaller panel.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You handle sensitive documents daily. The Peslv 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Screen gives a reversible face and a stated filtering figure, so you can tune glare and privacy.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need a filter for an occasional shared desk. The Computer Privacy Screen Filter 24 Inch 16:9 is enough for a single monitor.

faq.q: Do privacy screens work from directly behind me?
faq.a: No. A privacy filter narrows the side viewing angle only. The Computer Privacy Screen Filter listing itself notes it does not block visibility directly behind you.

faq.q: Will a privacy filter make my screen dimmer?
faq.a: Yes, a little. The micro-louver film reduces light at every angle, so you may raise brightness slightly. A matte coating also softens fine text.

faq.q: How do I know which size to buy?
faq.a: Measure the visible panel width and height without the bezel and compare to the listed dimensions, for example 532 by 299 mm for many 24-inch 16:9 panels.

faq.q: Is the Peslv worth it over the Mamol?
faq.a: If you want to test glossy and matte, yes, because the Peslv has a reversible surface. If you only care about fit, the Mamol's printed dimensions are enough.

faq.q: Can I use these on a touchscreen?
faq.a: The PYS laptop filter says it is not optimized for touchscreens, and the same caution applies to film filters in general. Test on a non-touch panel first.
They can slip on thin bezels. The hanging pair is meant to avoid adhesive, so check your bezel thickness before ordering.

finalTake: For most buyers the Vxaop 2-Pack 27 Inch is the answer: it states a 60 degree cone and a matte coating. On a 24-inch screen, the Peslv 2-Pack adds a reversible face. Fit-nervous buyers should lean on Mamol or Syhauifei, which print dimensions. Laptop users get the PYS magnetic filter.
